title: Custody death sparks inquest
article: Saskatchewan is launching an inquest into the death of a man who died in police custody two years ago, Regina police announced Thursday.
Scott Norman Schwager, 47, was found dead in his Regina prison cell on April 12, 2008.
He was arrested earlier that day for being drunk in public.
By law, an inquest must be held any time someone dies in police custody, unless the coroner is satisfied that the death was not preventable and was due to natural causes.
While there were no signs of rough play, the cause of death remains unknown.
A coroner's jury will investigate the cause of death and make recommendations on how to prevent the same thing from happening again.
The inquest is scheduled for March 8-12 in Regina.
